text: the Bible cannot interpret the Bible and when folks say we need to let the Bible interpret the Bible what they're really saying is you need to let me interpret
the Bible hey everybody I'm Dan mcclelen I'm a scholar of the Bible and religion and I see at least three main reasons the Bible cannot interpret the Bible the
first is that it cannot interpret anything because it is just a text it has no inherent meaning it cannot speak it cannot clarify it cannot correct it
cannot interpret it is a collection of squiggles and dashes and dots and meaning is only gener ated with those
squiggles and dashes and dots when they are engaged by a reader or readers within a specific set of circumstances
and those readers and their circumstances are going to be the proximate cause of whatever meaning is generated second main reason is that the
Bible is not univocal the notion that it can interpret itself requires we impose this presupposition of univocality the
notion the text speaks with a single unified and consistent voice from a single unified and consistent perspective and that presupposition is
not supported by any data whatsoever it's just a Dogma that one must choose to accept and then it is imposed upon
the text third main reason is that to have the Bible interpret the Bible we're going to have to compare texts we're going to have to bring other texts to
bear on our interpretation of a given text and sometimes those texts are going to have nothing to do with each other they may be separated by almost a
thousand years May entirely disagree with each other but to have the Bible interpret the Bible we've got to impose
requirements on the text regarding what it is and is not allowed to say and we've got to compel texts to agree with
each other which is going to either require we impose principles upon the text that subordinate all of them to those principles or we've got to pick
which texts are going to take priority and which texts are going to be subordinated all of that comes from the outside
Again by readers in order to turn the text into something that is Meaningful and useful to them in their specific set
of circumstances so across all of these considerations the real Authority is not the Bible the Bible is just a proof text
a symbolic Authority a Figure Head the real Authority is the ideologies the dogmas the traditions of the reader or
readers in their specific set of circumstances that determines how the Bible is interpreted the Bible does not
interpret itself
